CVE-2026-107493.title: Use-After-Free in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() when appending to a caller-supplied stack fails
CVE-2026-107493.description:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack.…

CVE-2026-118776.title: Forge: Incomplete PKCS#7 padding validation in AES/DES CBC and ECB decryption
CVE-2026-118776.description: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, the affected implementation used decipher.finish(), CBC and ECB modes, PKCS#7 padding to process the relevant input or security decision. node-forge validated only the final byte of PKCS#7 padding during CBC and ECB decryption and accepted zero, oversized, or mismatched padding bytes. CVE-2026-123824.description:
The Symfony Config component XmlUtils::parse() enables DTD validation before rejecting documents that carry a doctype, allowing XML external entity (XXE) injection in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. A remote attacker who can supply XML to this method can determine whether local files exist, cause a denial of service, and, in some configurations, exfiltrate local file content via a crafted XML document whose doctype declares an external file:// entity.
XmlUtils::parse() sets $dom->validateOnParse = true before calling loadXML() and only rejects documents carrying a doctype afterwards. Enabling DTD validation makes libxml resolve external entities during loadXML(), and LIBXML_NONET blocks http:// but not file://, so a file:// entity is read from disk before the doctype rejection runs. CVE-2026-63634.title: pympp: Gas Draining with padding
CVE-2026-63634.description: pympp is a Python SDK for the Machine Payments Protocol. Prior to version 0.9.1, when the server acts as the fee_payer, pympp validates calldata using eth_abi decoding, which is lenient about trailing bytes. The FeePayerPolicy caps gas_limit (≤ 2 M) and max_fee_per_gas (≤ 100 Gwei) but does not check calldata length. Tempo uses legacy calldata gas pricing: 16 gas per non-zero byte. Appending N bytes of 0x01 padding inflates actual gas used by N × 16 while keeping gas_limit and max_fee_per_gas within policy caps. The server cosigns and broadcasts the padded transaction, draining its fee-payer wallet. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.1.

CVE-2026-99194.title: net: ethernet: aeroflex: move setting of netops to fix crash
CVE-2026-99194.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ethernet: aeroflex: move setting of netops to fix crash

greth_of_probe() calls greth_mdio_init(), which connects the PHY,
before dev->netdev_ops is assigned. phy_attach_direct() ->
phy_link_topo_add_phy() reads dev->netdev_ops through
netdev_need_ops_lock() since the commit in question, so probing crashes
with a NULL pointer dereference when CONFIG_NET_SHAPER is enabled.

Assign netdev_ops before the PHY attach, as was done for emac in commit
7c9f391ec89c ("net: emac: move setting of netops to fix crash").

CVE-2026-99532.title: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic
CVE-2026-99532.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic

parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL pointers by adding untrusted
32-bit offsets to the security descriptor before checking their bounds.
The existing checks reject offsets into the descriptor header, but do
not reject offsets beyond the descriptor's length.

On a 32-bit kernel, a large offset can wrap the pointer before the
descriptor. The end-only checks in parse_sid() and parse_dacl() can then
accept it, allowing an authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request to access
memory outside the security descriptor and fault the kernel.

Check each nonzero offset against acl_len before constructing its
pointer. Initialize the optional owner and group SID pointers to NULL
so an omitted SID remains absent when parsing the DACL.

thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug

When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch
subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its
child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an
attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM
completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not
guaranteed numerically sorted).

seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I

that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found
that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault
at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went
bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()`…

CVE-2026-99763.title: 9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink
CVE-2026-99763.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink

A 9P2000.L server can report nlink=0 for a regular file that still
exists. On a cache=loose or cache=fscache mount, lookup stores that
value with set_nlink(). A later successful unlink calls
v9fs_dec_count(), which still calls drop_nlink() for a non-directory.
drop_nlink() warns, and the unsigned link count wraps to 4294967295.
fstat() on a descriptor opened before the unlink shows 0 before and
4294967295 after.
